newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Immigration officials at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport have tightened their screening of arriving foreigners, closely watching for suspected terrorists especially hit men of the Japanese Red Army, who may be targetting North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop. (INQUIRER)

- Congress will be the next battlefield for those pushing for Charter change and lifting the term limits on President Fidel Ramos and other elected officials. This warning was aired by Representative Ronaldo Zamora, House minority floor leader. (INQUIRER/STANDARD)

- The government has given up its claim on the Marcoses' 450 million-peso Swiss deposits in order to give free rein to some 10,000 human rights victims who had won a $2.0 billion damage suit in the United States against the Marcoses, Solicitor General Silvestre Bello told reporters in a telephone interview from the Netherlands. (TIMES/INQUIRER)
- The Philippines' unemployment rate last January fell to 7.7 percent from 8.3 percent in the year-ago period, the National Statistics Office reported yesterday (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Andres Soriano and Carlos Soriano, chairman and vice-chairman of A. Soriano Corp, issued a joint statement downplaying the alleged rift over the management of the company. (CHRONICLE)

- Food and beverage giant San Miguel Corp, Solid Banking Corp and Dharmala Group of Indonesia are putting up a firm to control 60 percent of the soon to be privatised state-owned Philippine International Trading Corp (PITC), said Jose Luis Yulo, PITC president.
